title: 100 Years of Balloons: Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade Marks Its 100th March Thursday
excerpt: The 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade marches Thursday at 8:30 a.m. on NBC and Peacock, with a record 100 inflatables, RAYE opening and a nine-show Broadway medley.
content:
One hundred years after the first march down Manhattan, the Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade returns Thursday, November 26, for its 100th parade — and this one is built to be the biggest the holiday has ever seen.

The parade steps off at 8:30 a.m. in all time zones and runs until noon, airing live on NBC and streaming on Peacock, with a Spanish-language broadcast on Telemundo and an encore on NBC at 2 p.m. ET/PT. It travels its familiar 2.5-mile route from West 77th Street and Central Park West down to Macy's Herald Square, where Santa Claus traditionally closes the show.

The first parade was held in 1924. The 100th march lands in 2026, not 2024, because the parade was canceled in 1942, 1943 and 1944 during World War II. More than 11,000 volunteers will bring this year's parade to life, and more than 3 million spectators are expected along the route.

A record 100 inflatables

This year's parade will feature a record-breaking 100 inflatable elements, including new balloons of Bluey, Hello Kitty, Sorcerer's Apprentice Mickey, Joe Cool and Woodstock from Peanuts, Underdog, Buckaroo Bob the Minion riding a giant banana, Earl the Squirrel, and Billie Brightpaw, a bear created by Macy's Studios. New floats include Hogwarts Holiday from HBO, Tony Sarg's Amazing Marionettes, a Macy's Parade All-Stars float, Mr. Peanut Power Plant, Purina Dog Chow Salute to Service Dogs, and GEICO's Road Trip to Parade.

Who is performing

RAYE, the leader in 2027 Grammy nominations, will open the broadcast, joined by her sisters Amma and Absolutely. Megan Moroney and Teddy Swims will deliver the featured performances at Herald Square, and Megan Hilty will lead a special tribute to Dolly Parton. The lineup also includes Queen Latifah, Jimmy Fallon & The Roots, Feid, DEVO, Baha Men, Natasha Bedingfield, Keke Palmer, Mckenna Grace, Leslie Odom Jr., Anthony Ramos, RIIZE, Smash Mouth, the Indigo Girls, Icona Pop, JoJo, Wyclef Jean, Il Volo and Natalie Merchant. The Radio City Rockettes will also join the broadcast.

The TODAY show's Savannah Guthrie, Hoda Kotb and Al Roker return as hosts of the NBC broadcast.

Nine Broadway shows, one medley

In a one-time-only performance, the casts of nine Broadway musicals — The Book of Mormon, Chicago, Disney's Aladdin, Hamilton, The Lost Boys, Rent, Richard O'Brien's The Rocky Horror Show, Schmigadoon! and Wicked — will unite for a 10-minute medley honoring Broadway, introduced by Julianne Hough. The Schmigadoon! cast has been rehearsing for the parade, part of the show's turn in the spotlight as it heads toward a Broadway transfer.

How to watch from Laredo

The celebration starts tonight: NBC's Countdown to Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade airs Wednesday, November 25, at 8 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock, hosted by Jack McBrayer, with a look inside the Macy's Parade Studio and interviews with performers Mckenna Grace and Leslie Odom Jr. A new documentary, America's Parade: 100 Years of Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, aired November 20 on NBC and is now streaming on Peacock. For blind and low-vision viewers, the NBC broadcast will include live audio description on the Secondary Audio Program channel.

What it means

Analysis: A century in, the parade has become the most-watched entertainment program of the year on broadcast television, according to NBCUniversal — a shared morning ritual that survives every shift in how America watches TV. The 100th edition leans into that history with the record balloon count and the nine-show Broadway medley, while the new floats and the RAYE opening show the parade still chasing the next generation of viewers. For Laredo families gathering Thursday morning, the turkey can wait — the balloons start at 8:30.
